justifications.text: This 48-year-old female with multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, family history of early CVD, prior angina) presenting with acute-onset heavy chest pain radiating to bilateral shoulders and arms, associated with dyspnea and exertional pattern requires urgent escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome.

This patient presents with acute anaphylaxis or severe allergic reaction (urticaria, dyspnea, wheezing, dizziness, nausea, facial flushing) requiring immediate clinical assessment and potential emergency intervention.

This 66-year-old with chronic pancreatitis, smoking history, obesity, family history of pancreatic cancer, and new presentation of diarrhea, left flank pain, epigastric yellow lesion, and pale stools with dark urine requires urgent escalation to exclude pancreatic malignancy.

This patient presents with a classic acute dystonic reaction (oculogyric crisis, trismus, facial spasms, dysphagia, dyspnea) following recent antipsychotic initiation and recent parenteral medication administration, which requires urgent medical evaluation and likely requires immediate treatment with an anticholinergic agent.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to acute onset of progressive neurological symptoms (facial weakness, bilateral limb weakness, paresthesias, dyspnea) following viral infection, highly suggestive of Guillain-Barré syndrome, which carries risk of respiratory failure and requires immediate specialist evaluation and potential ICU monitoring.

This patient presents with multi-system features consistent with acute allergic reaction (known severe food allergy, contact exposure, urticaria, angioedema, dyspnea, dizziness, GI symptoms) and requires urgent clinical assessment to rule out anaphylaxis or severe systemic allergic response.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to fever, bleeding/bruising, confusion, dyspnea, and fatigue following recent West African travel with known contact to similarly symptomatic individuals, raising concern for viral hemorrhagic fever including Ebola.

This 82-year-old with known asthma, recent hospitalization for asthma attack, multiple attacks in the past year, and current acute presentation of dyspnea, cough, and wheezing requires urgent clinician evaluation to assess for acute asthma exacerbation and rule out other serious cardiopulmonary pathology.

This 64-year-old with multiple cardiac risk factors (HIV, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prior angina, family history, poor circulation) presenting with acute-onset severe chest pain radiating to bilateral shoulders and arms, diaphoresis, dyspnea, and constitutional symptoms requires immediate escalation to rule out acute myocardial infarction.
High-pitched inspiratory stridor in a patient with asthma history and daily secondhand smoke exposure warrants urgent clinician assessment to rule out acute asthma exacerbation or airway obstruction.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to chest pain with dyspnea, palpitations, and recent viral infection raising concern for myocarditis or acute coronary syndrome, both potentially life-threatening conditions.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to high-risk features for pulmonary embolism (hemoptysis, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, bilateral calf swelling, recent immobility, surgery, travel, and active cancer), which is a life-threatening emergency.

This patient requires immediate escalation due to acute severe tearing chest and flank pain with rapid onset, bilateral scapular radiation, dyspnea, and hematemesis—classic presentation for aortic dissection, a life-threatening emergency.

This 63-year-old smoker with family history of lung cancer presents with hemoptysis, constitutional symptoms (fatigue, weight loss, anorexia), dyspnea, and persistent cough—a constellation highly concerning for malignancy requiring urgent investigation.

This 67-year-old dialysis patient with history of heart failure and prior MI presents with acute chest pain (multiple locations with radiation to arm/jaw/shoulder), dyspnea, diaphoresis, and exertional symptoms—concerning for acute coronary syndrome or acute decompensated heart failure requiring urgent evaluation.

This 80-year-old with multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, obesity, family history, prior angina) presenting with acute severe chest pain (10/10), diaphoresis, dyspnea, radiation to bilateral arms and neck, and exertional pattern requires immediate escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to acute onset severe headache with chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, and dizziness—concerning for acute coronary syndrome or other serious cardiopulmonary pathology, despite stimulant use as a contributing factor.

Acute pharyngitis is most likely, but the combination of stridor (high-pitched breathing), voice changes, and rapid onset with severe bilateral neck/throat pain warrants urgent assessment for croup or epiglottitis to exclude airway compromise, particularly given stimulant use and hypertension history.

Hemoptysis with systemic symptoms (fever, chills, fatigue), chest pain, and characteristic rash in an underweight young male smoker raises concern for pulmonary tuberculosis, requiring urgent investigation and isolation precautions.

66-year-old male with acute-onset severe chest pain (10/10) exacerbated by exertion and relieved by rest in multiple chest locations raises significant concern for acute coronary syndrome; immediate clinical evaluation and ECG are warranted.

This patient has multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, family history of early CAD) with exertional chest pain radiating to arm and jaw—classic angina presentation with acute coronary syndrome risk; urgent clinical evaluation and ECG are required.

This patient presents with widespread pink skin lesions across multiple body sites with significant pruritus but minimal pain, most consistent with urticaria or dermatitis; while concerning features are absent, the distribution and intensity warrant clinical evaluation to exclude systemic causes and guide appropriate management.

This 76-year-old with chronic pancreatitis, smoking history, weight loss, vague epigastric pain, and a yellow skin lesion has concerning features for pancreatic cancer that warrant urgent clinical evaluation and imaging.

This patient presents with classic acute dystonia (oculogyric crisis, lingual dystonia, torticollis, trismus) in the context of recent antipsychotic exposure and recent parenteral medication administration, requiring urgent evaluation and potential treatment with anticholinergic agents to prevent airway compromise.

This patient presents with acute-onset bilateral facial weakness, bilateral limb weakness, and paresthesias in a distal and perioral distribution following recent viral infection, highly suggestive of Guillain-Barré syndrome, which requires urgent neurological assessment and potential hospitalization to monitor for respiratory compromise.

This 18-year-old with known severe food allergy presents with acute onset (7/10) diffuse abdominal pain, facial/airway swelling, stridor, wheeze, urticarial rash, and presyncope—classic features of anaphylaxis requiring immediate escalation and emergency assessment.

This elderly patient presents with fever, cough, dyspnea, myalgia, nausea, bleeding/bruising, and confusion following recent West African travel and contact with a symptomatic person, raising concern for a serious communicable disease including viral hemorrhagic fever that requires immediate isolation and specialist evaluation.

This 63-year-old with known asthma, recent asthma attacks, and current acute dyspnea with wheezing requires urgent clinician assessment to rule out acute asthma exacerbation and evaluate for potential respiratory compromise.

This 65-year-old with significant cardiac risk factors (prior MI/angina, smoking history, obesity, family history, HIV) presenting with acute severe chest pain radiating to jaw, shoulders, and arms with diaphoresis and dyspnea requires urgent escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome.
Stridor (high-pitched breathing sound) warrants prompt evaluation to exclude upper airway obstruction or other potentially serious causes requiring urgent intervention.

This 51-year-old male presents with chest pain exacerbated by exertion and relieved by rest, accompanied by palpitations and fatigue, raising significant concern for angina pectoris which requires urgent clinical evaluation and possible cardiac workup.
Recent surgery, hormonal therapy, unilateral leg swelling, and pleuritic chest pain raise concern for pulmonary embolism, which requires urgent evaluation despite low pain intensity.

Acute chest pain with radiation to scapulae, dyspnea, and hematemesis in a 31-year-old requires urgent evaluation to exclude acute coronary syndrome despite young age, particularly given rapid onset and severity of presentation.

This 73-year-old smoker with hemoptysis, constitutional weight loss, chest pain, and strong family history of lung cancer requires urgent escalation for imaging and specialist evaluation to exclude malignancy.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to concerning features of acute pulmonary embolism: bilateral calf swelling with unilateral tibial swelling, acute dyspnea with orthopnea, chest pain with radiation pattern, and history of heart failure creating thromboembolism risk.

This 33-year-old with multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, family history of early CAD) presenting with progressive chest pain at rest, diaphoresis, fatigue, and radiation to bilateral arms and shoulder requires urgent escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome.
Young female presenting with dyspnea, palpitations, and irregular heartbeat requires urgent evaluation to exclude arrhythmia or other cardiac pathology despite likely anxiety-stimulant contribution.
Acute pharyngitis/pharyngeal pain with dysphagia, stridor, and hypersalivation requires urgent evaluation to exclude peritonsillar abscess or epiglottitis given respiratory symptoms and rapid onset.

Hemoptysis with chest pain, dyspnea, and constitutional symptoms in a 52-year-old smoker with COPD history raises significant concern for lung malignancy and requires urgent clinical evaluation and imaging.

Acute aortic dissection must be ruled out urgently given the sudden onset of severe tearing/stabbing chest pain (9/10) with rapid onset, pleuritic features, and risk factors including age and smoking history.

This 41-year-old with multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, family history of early CAD) presenting with severe (9/10) chest pain radiating to arm and shoulder, exertional in nature and relieved by rest, requires urgent escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome.

Patient presents with systemic symptoms (lightheadedness, nausea, palpitations, flushing) alongside widespread urticarial lesions with significant pruritus, suggesting possible acute allergic reaction or urticaria with cardiovascular involvement; cardiac arrhythmia flagged due to reported palpitations and tachycardia requiring evaluation.

This 63-year-old diabetic patient with obesity presents with diarrhea, epigastric/left hypochondrial cramping pain, fatigue, and a yellow skin lesion, raising concern for gastritis or peptic ulcer disease which requires clinical evaluation to exclude serious gastrointestinal pathology.

This patient presents with acute dystonic features (oculogyric crisis, torticollis, trismus, facial spasms, dyspnea) following recent hospitalization with parenteral medication administration, highly suggestive of acute dystonia—a medical emergency requiring immediate intervention.

This elderly patient presents with acute bilateral weakness, facial involvement, paresthesias, and respiratory compromise—a constellation highly concerning for Guillain-Barré syndrome, which requires urgent escalation for potential respiratory support and immunotherapy.

This patient requires clinician evaluation due to concerning chest pain characteristics (stabbing, burning, radiating to upper chest) with multiple cardiac risk factors (age 52, male, smoking, excessive alcohol use) that warrant urgent assessment to exclude acute coronary syndrome or hypertensive emergency.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to multiple cardiac risk factors (valve disease, heart defect, prior MI/angina, hypertension, diabetes, obesity) presenting with acute dyspnea, palpitations, and exertional symptoms concerning for acute heart failure or arrhythmia.

Acute pericarditis is most likely given recent viral infection, history of prior pericarditis, pleuritic chest pain with radiation to back, and dyspnea; this requires urgent evaluation to exclude tamponade or myopericarditis.

This patient presents with a constellation of symptoms highly suggestive of myasthenia gravis (bulbar weakness, ptosis, generalized weakness worsening with fatigue, dyspnea), which requires urgent evaluation and potential respiratory monitoring given the respiratory involvement.

This patient with known COPD and recent flare-ups presenting with productive cough and wheezing requires urgent clinician assessment to evaluate for acute COPD exacerbation and rule out infectious complications.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to symptomatic anemia (fatigue, dizziness, pallor, hematochezia) complicated by chronic kidney failure and recent West African travel, with significant risk for iron deficiency or infectious causes requiring immediate investigation.

A 99-year-old smoker with hemoptysis, severe pharyngeal pain, and cough requires urgent escalation to exclude malignancy or other serious pulmonary pathology despite infectious symptoms being present.

Acute onset severe chest pain with pleuritic features and cough requires urgent evaluation to exclude acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or other serious cardiopulmonary pathology despite musculoskeletal features.

This 61-year-old male with multiple chest pain locations, palpitations, dizziness, and anxiety symptoms requires urgent cardiac evaluation to exclude arrhythmia or acute coronary syndrome despite low pain intensity and anxiety history.

Acute pharyngitis/tonsillitis with fever and bilateral tonsillar pain is the most likely diagnosis; flagging acute tonsillitis as it may require assessment for complications (peritonsillar abscess) or need for antibiotics if bacterial, particularly given household crowding and smoking status.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to the combination of hemoptysis, dyspnea, fever, constitutional symptoms (weight loss), and underweight status in a 59-year-old, raising significant concern for malignancy or serious pulmonary infection.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to multiple cardiac red flags including palpitations, dyspnea on exertion, pre-existing valvular disease, and history of angina/MI, raising concern for acute myocarditis or decompensated valvular disease.

This 62-year-old woman with recent viral infection, history of pericarditis, sharp chest pain radiating to thoracic spine, dyspnea, and positional relief with sitting up has clinical features highly suggestive of acute pericarditis, which requires urgent evaluation to exclude complications such as tamponade or constrictive physiology.

This young female presents with a classic triad of myasthenia gravis (ptosis, dysarthria, and proximal weakness worsened by fatigue), requiring urgent neurological evaluation and antibody testing to confirm diagnosis and initiate appropriate treatment.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to severe pleuritic chest pain (9/10) with rapid onset in the context of known metastatic cancer, raising concern for malignant pleural involvement, pulmonary embolism, or spontaneous pneumothorax.

This patient presents with classic allergic rhinitis symptoms (nasal itching, congestion, clear rhinorrhea) with significant risk factors including family history of asthma and predisposition to allergies; no red flags for serious pathology are present, so routine clinical assessment is appropriate.

Acute bilateral lower limb swelling and pain in a patient with known heart failure and cirrhosis suggests decompensated heart failure or hepatic decompensation, both requiring urgent clinical assessment and investigation.

The combination of polyarticular joint pain (neck, ankle, wrist, knee), facial rash with oral ulcers, and dyspnea suggests possible systemic inflammatory or autoimmune disease requiring urgent clinical evaluation and investigation.

This patient presents with acute respiratory symptoms (cough with sputum, fever, sore throat, nasal congestion) in the context of recent exposure to similar illness and occupational/household crowding; acute bronchitis warrants clinical assessment to exclude lower respiratory tract involvement and assess for complications given smoking history.
This patient with COPD presenting with productive cough, fever, and chest pain requires escalation to rule out bacterial pneumonia, which carries significant morbidity risk in this population.

This 72-year-old with chronic kidney failure, poor diet, family history of anemia, and presenting with bilateral temporal headache, dyspnea, dizziness, fatigue, and pallor has a high probability of iron deficiency anemia requiring urgent investigation and management to prevent complications.

Herpes zoster (shingles) involving the trigeminal nerve distribution requires prompt antiviral treatment if confirmed, as early intervention significantly improves outcomes in this elderly patient with dermatomal pain pattern and recent viral illness.
Acute otitis media with fever is the most likely diagnosis and warrants prompt assessment to rule out complications and determine need for antibiotic therapy.

This patient requires clinician assessment due to multi-site pharyngeal pain (7/10), fever, cough, hoarseness, and high-risk exposure setting; while acute upper respiratory infection is most likely, croup (J05.0) must be excluded given the constellation of symptoms including voice changes and potential airway involvement.

This 64-year-old male presents with severe (9/10) stabbing chest pain radiating to the back with palpitations and positional features suggestive of pericarditis, but acute coronary syndrome cannot be excluded given age, pain severity, and cardiac symptoms, requiring urgent clinical evaluation and ECG.

68-year-old with history of asthma presenting with wheeze, intense coughing fits, and post-tussive vomiting requires urgent assessment for acute asthma exacerbation or other lower airway obstruction to rule out serious respiratory compromise.

This immunosuppressed patient with bilateral tonsillar and pharyngeal pain in a high-transmission setting (daycare, household crowding) requires prompt evaluation to exclude acute bacterial tonsillitis or peritonsillar abscess, which carry risk of airway compromise and systemic complications in immunocompromised hosts.

This patient presents with classic panic attack symptoms (acute onset, dyspnea, chest pain, diaphoresis, dizziness, paresthesias, fear of dying) in the context of chronic anxiety and depression; while organic causes must be excluded, the constellation of symptoms and psychiatric history strongly suggests acute anxiety disorder requiring urgent clinical assessment to rule out cardiac or other serious pathology.

This 107-year-old patient presents with multi-site burning/sharp pain, diffuse eye redness, and vaginal discharge following recent North American travel, raising concern for rubella or other systemic viral infection requiring urgent evaluation to rule out serious infectious disease in an elderly patient.

This elderly patient presents with unilateral orbital pain, facial pain distribution across trigeminal nerve territories, and anosmia; while chronic sinusitis is most likely given nasal history, trigeminal neuralgia or other neurological causes warrant urgent evaluation to exclude serious pathology in this age group.

This 103-year-old with strong allergic predisposition (family history, asthma, living in city) presenting with ocular pruritus and rhinitis most likely has allergic conjunctivitis or seasonal allergic rhinitis; no red flags for acute infection or serious pathology identified in intake.

Bilateral ankle and lower limb swelling with weight gain in a patient with known heart failure and kidney disease (proteinuria) suggests decompensated heart failure with fluid retention, requiring urgent clinical assessment and possible intervention.

The constellation of polyarticular joint pain (neck, wrists, ankle), bilateral symmetric involvement, oral ulcers, facial erythema, and dyspnea raises concern for systemic lupus erythematosus or other connective tissue disease, warranting urgent rheumatologic evaluation and serologic testing.

This patient presents with classic viral upper respiratory infection symptoms (fever, sore throat, nasal congestion, cough with sputum, myalgia, diaphoresis) with recent exposure to similar illness in a daycare setting; while concerning features like headache and smoking history are present, the clinical picture is consistent with common viral illness and does not require immediate escalation, though examination and vital signs should be obtained to exclude complications.

This patient with known COPD presenting with acute respiratory symptoms (cough, sputum production, fever, dyspnea, sore throat, nasal congestion) requires clinician evaluation to assess for COPD exacerbation or acute lower respiratory infection, which could warrant escalation of care.

This patient requires urgent clinician review due to suspected pregnancy combined with anemia, dyspnea, dizziness, and pallor—a potentially dangerous combination requiring immediate assessment and investigation.

This elderly patient with smoking history and nasal polyps presents with classic acute sinusitis (facial pain, purulent nasal discharge, anosmia); no red flags for emergent conditions identified, but clinician should assess for complications given age and comorbidities.

Herpes zoster oticus (shingles of the ear) requires prompt recognition in an elderly patient due to risk of complications including Ramsay Hunt syndrome; the bilateral ear tenderness with recent mood changes warrants clinical assessment to rule out this condition.

Croup (J05.0) should be flagged given the combination of hoarseness, cough, and recent upper respiratory infection in a young adult with close contact exposure, though acute pharyngitis is more likely; escalation recommended to confirm diagnosis and assess airway status.

Acute myocardial infarction must be excluded urgently given severe chest pain (8/10) with rapid onset, radiation pattern, and pleuritic features in a 46-year-old male, despite pericarditis being more likely given recent viral infection and positional/pleuritic characteristics.
Recent pertussis exposure with intense coughing fits and post-tussive vomiting raises significant concern for pertussis infection, which requires prompt confirmation and public health notification.

This patient presents with classic viral pharyngitis symptoms (bilateral pharyngeal pain, fever, cough, nasal congestion) in a high-transmission setting; no red flags for severe infection or complications are evident, so routine management is appropriate.

This patient presents with classic panic attack symptoms (dyspnea, choking sensation, fear of dying, paresthesias, depersonalization) in the context of anxiety, depression, and alcohol use disorder, requiring urgent assessment to rule out medical causes and initiate appropriate psychiatric/medical management.

Loss of consciousness with violent sustained muscle contractions suggests a seizure disorder, which requires urgent clinical evaluation and investigation to rule out epilepsy or other serious neurological conditions.

This patient presents with classic sinusitis symptoms (facial pain with bilateral distribution, nasal discharge, anosmia) in the context of predisposing factors (nasal polyps, allergies, asthma); no red flags for serious pathology are evident, but clinician assessment is warranted to confirm diagnosis and rule out complications.

This patient presents with classic allergic symptoms (nasal/pharyngeal itching, ocular pruritus, cough) with significant asthma risk factors (family history, personal history of bronchodilator use, allergic predisposition); asthma exacerbation or new-onset asthma requires clinical assessment to rule out lower airway involvement.

Acute bilateral lower limb swelling with pain in a patient with known heart failure and liver cirrhosis requires urgent assessment for decompensated heart failure or hepatic decompensation, both potentially life-threatening conditions.

This patient requires clinician escalation due to the constellation of polyarticular joint pain (bilateral ankles, wrists, neck), malar rash, dyspnea, and history of pericarditis, which raises concern for systemic lupus erythematosus or other connective tissue disease requiring urgent serological evaluation and specialist referral.

This 74-year-old presents with systemic symptoms (fever, myalgia, sweating) and respiratory findings (productive cough, sore throat, nasal congestion) consistent with influenza in a high-risk elderly patient with recent exposure; requires prompt evaluation for antiviral eligibility and complications.

Patient with known COPD presenting with acute respiratory symptoms including productive cough, wheezing, dyspnea, and chest pain requires urgent clinician assessment to rule out COPD exacerbation or secondary respiratory infection.

This patient requires urgent clinician review due to chronic kidney failure combined with anemia, dizziness, fatigue, and pallor—suggesting possible severe anemia or CKD-related complications requiring immediate assessment and laboratory investigation.

Severe facial pain (8/10) with purulent nasal discharge, anosmia, and recent upper respiratory infection strongly suggests acute sinusitis, which requires prompt evaluation to exclude complications and guide appropriate treatment.

This patient requires clinician evaluation due to right ear pain with fever and cough, suggesting possible acute otitis media or suppurative otitis media, which may require examination and imaging to rule out complications.

This patient presents with acute pharyngitis with hoarseness in a high-transmission setting (daycare worker, crowded household); symptoms are consistent with common viral or bacterial pharyngitis and do not currently suggest a condition requiring urgent escalation, though clinical examination is needed to assess severity and guide management.

Intense coughing with post-tussive vomiting in a vaccinated patient without asthma history suggests acute viral bronchitis or upper respiratory infection; no red flags for immediate escalation identified, but clinician assessment recommended to exclude pertussis or other serious causes.

This immunocompromised patient with HIV, corticosteroid use, low BMI, and the classic triad of fever, cough, and dyspnea has a high probability of Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), a serious opportunistic infection requiring urgent evaluation and treatment.

This 94-year-old immunosuppressed patient presents with dermatomal headache/neck pain, unilateral pink skin lesion on right neck, fever, chills, and systemic symptoms highly suggestive of herpes zoster; requires urgent evaluation and antiviral therapy to prevent complications.

Trigeminal neuralgia presents with severe lancinating facial pain in trigeminal distribution and requires urgent neurological evaluation to exclude secondary causes and initiate appropriate treatment; however, cluster headache with autonomic features (lacrimation, nasal congestion) is also highly likely and warrants prompt assessment to guide management.

This 68-year-old with multiple HIV risk factors (unprotected sex with multiple partners, sexual contact with HIV-positive partner, IV drug use, prior STI history) presenting with lymphadenopathy, fever, sore throat, fatigue, and oral/genital lesions requires urgent HIV testing and specialist evaluation for acute retroviral syndrome or advanced HIV disease.
Black stools (melena) suggest upper GI bleeding, which requires urgent evaluation to rule out active hemorrhage despite moderate pain intensity and gradual onset.
Acute onset bloating with bilateral iliac/hip pain, inability to pass stools/gas, and rapid symptom onset raises concern for bowel obstruction, which requires urgent clinical evaluation and imaging.

This patient presents with a classic triad of myasthenia gravis (jaw weakness, diplopia, dysarthria) plus dysphagia and dyspnea with fatigue-related worsening, requiring urgent escalation to rule out this potentially life-threatening condition and assess for respiratory compromise.

This patient requires clinician evaluation due to the combination of severe headache (8/10) with fever, nausea, and systemic symptoms (fatigue, weight loss, myalgias) that could indicate meningitis or other serious infection, despite the gradual onset.
Acute bronchitis with severe pleuritic chest pain and intense coughing in a young patient requires prompt evaluation to exclude more serious respiratory pathology and assess for complications.

This patient with severe COPD and recent exacerbations presenting with acute dyspnea, cough, and wheezing requires urgent clinician assessment to rule out acute COPD exacerbation or other serious respiratory complications.

This immunosuppressed patient with cystic fibrosis, COPD, and history of pneumonia presenting with hemoptysis, dyspnea, and productive cough requires urgent escalation to rule out acute pneumonia or other serious pulmonary infection.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to hemoptysis with dyspnea in the context of IV drug use and immunocompromise (underweight, diabetes, substance abuse), raising significant concern for opportunistic infection including PCP pneumonia, which carries high morbidity if untreated.

This patient requires clinician escalation due to the combination of severe headache (8/10), fever, chills, myalgia, rash, and recent North American travel, raising concern for Lyme disease or other tick-borne illness that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to severe acute facial pain (9/10) with lancinating/stabbing character, precise localization, rapid onset, and bilateral trigeminal distribution suggesting possible cluster headache or trigeminal neuralgia, both requiring prompt specialist evaluation and management.

This 68-year-old with recent high-risk sexual exposure (unprotected sex with HIV-positive partner) presenting with fever, lymphadenopathy, oral ulcers, genital lesions, diarrhea, and systemic symptoms concerning for acute HIV infection or other serious immunocompromising condition requiring urgent testing and specialist evaluation.
Black stools (melena) suggest upper GI bleeding, which requires urgent evaluation to rule out active hemorrhage or severe gastric ulceration despite relatively low pain intensity.

This 72-year-old presents with abdominal distension, localized pain in multiple sites, pale skin lesions >1cm over iliac fossae, and intense coughing; the combination warrants urgent evaluation to exclude serious pathology such as malignancy, obstruction, or systemic disease.

This patient presents with a constellation of neurological symptoms including facial/jaw weakness, dysarthria, dysphagia, and dyspnea suggesting possible motor neuron disease or other serious neurological condition requiring urgent specialist evaluation.

This 62-year-old presents with multi-location headache (bilateral temples, forehead, occipital, cervical), fever, diarrhea, weight loss, and constitutional symptoms; while most likely tension or viral headache, the combination warrants clinician assessment to exclude serious causes such as meningitis, temporal arteritis, or systemic infection.

This patient with known metastatic cancer presenting with acute severe pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and cough requires urgent escalation to rule out life-threatening complications such as malignant pleural effusion, pulmonary embolism, or pneumothorax.

This patient with history of heart failure and angina presents with acute multi-focal chest pain radiating to jaw/shoulder, dyspnea, orthopnea, and systemic symptoms including bilateral lower limb swelling and fatigue; acute coronary syndrome or acute decompensated heart failure requires urgent evaluation.

This patient requires urgent clinician assessment due to acute shortness of breath and cough in the context of poorly controlled asthma (≥2 attacks in past year with recent hospitalization), recent upper respiratory infection, and daily secondhand smoke exposure, raising concern for acute asthma exacerbation.

This patient requires immediate escalation due to high probability of acute aortic dissection, presenting with classic features: sudden-onset severe tearing pain (9/10) radiating to back/scapulae, spanning chest to abdomen, with dyspnea and hematemesis, necessitating emergency imaging and cardiothoracic evaluation.

This patient requires urgent clinician escalation due to concerning features for lung malignancy: active smoking history, family history of lung cancer, unexplained weight loss over 3 months, persistent cough, and localized chest wall pain—a combination warranting prompt investigation including imaging.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to high-risk epidemiological exposure (West Africa travel, contact with symptomatic person) combined with a constellation of symptoms (confusion, fatigue, myalgia, nausea, bleeding/bruising, cough) highly concerning for Ebola virus disease, which demands immediate isolation and specialist evaluation.

This 80-year-old presents with severe headache (7/10) with palpitations and dizziness; cardiac arrhythmia must be excluded urgently given age and symptom constellation, despite stimulant use being a likely contributor.

This patient has multiple high-risk factors for venous thromboembolism (active cancer, prior DVT, recent surgery, recent travel) with bilateral lower extremity swelling and chest pain concerning for pulmonary embolism, requiring urgent escalation and imaging.

This 38-year-old with multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, smoking, obesity, family history of early CVD, prior angina) presenting with severe 9/10 chest pain radiating to bilateral arms, shoulders, and thoracic spine with dyspnea and fatigue requires urgent escalation to rule out acute coronary syndrome or myocardial infarction.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to concerning features for pancreatic cancer: chronic pancreatitis, unexplained weight loss, pale stools with dark urine (suggesting biliary obstruction), left-sided flank pain, smoking history, obesity, and family history of pancreatic cancer.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation for acute coronary syndrome; she presents with severe (7/10) chest pain with radiation to jaw and bilateral arms, dyspnea, and fatigue in the context of multiple cardiac risk factors (HIV, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, prior angina, family history of early CAD, and poor circulation).

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to acute pharyngitis/tonsillitis with fever, significant dyspnea, and voice changes, which raises concern for severe infection or potential airway compromise.

Acute dyspnea with sensation of suffocation in a 67-year-old with recent hospitalization and stimulant use raises concern for acute decompensated heart failure or cardiac event, requiring urgent clinical evaluation.

This patient requires urgent clinician assessment due to concurrent respiratory symptoms (shortness of breath, wheezing, lightheadedness) with widespread pruritic skin lesions, suggesting possible acute asthma exacerbation or anaphylaxis that needs immediate evaluation.

Herpes zoster is highly likely given the dermatomal distribution of vesicular rash (thoracic/flank), stabbing chest wall pain, and constitutional symptoms; requires prompt antiviral treatment and close monitoring given patient's comorbidities (heart failure, Parkinson's disease).

This patient requires urgent escalation due to high-risk features for acute coronary syndrome: progressive chest pain with radiation to jaw and bilateral arms, dyspnea, fatigue, and multiple cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, obesity, family history, prior angina), with worsening symptoms over 2 weeks and decreasing effort threshold.

Hemoptysis in an immunosuppressed patient with COPD and prior pneumonia raises concern for serious lower respiratory infection including bacterial pneumonia, requiring urgent clinical evaluation and imaging.

Acute chest pain with diaphoresis, palpitations, and dizziness in a 50-year-old male warrants urgent evaluation to exclude acute coronary syndrome despite anxiety history and multiple psychosomatic features.

This patient with COPD presenting with acute cough, fever, sore throat, and colored sputum suggests acute bronchitis or respiratory infection requiring clinical assessment to rule out pneumonia and guide appropriate management.

This patient requires urgent escalation due to a constellation of findings highly suggestive of advanced HIV infection: multiple risk factors (IV drug use, unprotected sex with multiple partners, prior STI), oral ulceration with pale lesions, genital lesions, pharyngitis, diarrhea, weight loss, and systemic symptoms—warranting immediate HIV testing and specialist referral.

This patient presents with acute pharyngitis with concurrent laryngitis following recent upper respiratory infection; symptoms are consistent with viral etiology and self-limiting course, but clinical assessment is needed to exclude bacterial infection or epiglottitis given multi-site throat involvement and voice changes.

This HIV-positive patient with hemoptysis, dyspnea, and low BMI has a high probability of opportunistic infection (PCP) requiring urgent investigation and possible hospitalization to prevent respiratory compromise.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to acute pleuritic chest pain with dyspnea, palpitations, and tachycardia following recent viral infection, with history of prior pericarditis, raising concern for recurrent pericarditis or myopericarditis.

This patient requires clinician escalation due to acute exacerbation of known COPD with productive cough and wheezing in the context of recent flare-ups, necessitating assessment for infection, medication adjustment, and potential need for respiratory support.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to severe, acute-onset chest pain (9/10) with violent, tearing character in the context of metastatic cancer, raising concern for malignant involvement, pathological fracture, or other life-threatening thoracic pathology.

This patient presents with a classic triad of myasthenia gravis (diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia) plus ptosis, proximal weakness, and fatigue-related symptom exacerbation; requires urgent neurological evaluation and antibody testing to confirm diagnosis and initiate treatment.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to acute dyspnea, palpitations, and exertional chest symptoms in the context of significant cardiac risk factors (prior MI/angina, heart defect, hypertension, diabetes) and hyperthyroidism; acute coronary syndrome must be excluded.
Hemoptysis with pharyngeal pain and immunosuppression raises concern for croup or other serious airway pathology requiring urgent evaluation to exclude malignancy or severe infection.

This patient requires urgent clinician evaluation due to severe (9/10) multi-location chest and abdominal pain with biliary colic features (right hypochondriac tenderness, post-prandial worsening) and risk factors including alcohol use; acute cholecystitis or pancreatitis must be excluded.

This 62-year-old male presents with constitutional symptoms (unintentional weight loss, fatigue, loss of appetite), cervical lymphadenopathy, and dyspnea, raising concern for malignancy; lung cancer warrants urgent evaluation given age, smoking risk profile, and symptom constellation.
Hemoptysis with dyspnea in an immunosuppressed Asian patient with cystic fibrosis and prior pneumonia raises concern for tuberculosis, which requires urgent investigation and isolation precautions.

This patient has multiple cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, family history of early CAD, prior angina/MI) with acute onset chest pain radiating to shoulders and arms, dyspnea, and exertional pattern—concerning for acute coronary syndrome rather than panic attack, requiring urgent cardiac evaluation.
